To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a double-prism beam expander in the cavity of a rhodamine 6G dye laser, pumped by a copper vapor laser, leads to a 2–3-fold reduction in the linewidth of the laser output, compared to that obtained without the double prism, and that the linewidth can be reduced to 1.2 GHz at a pulse repetition rate of 5 kHz.
narrow-linewidth, high-repetition-frequency copper laser-pumped laser oscillators can be designed to operate efficiently and reliably over a wide range of operating conditions.

high repetition-rate copper laser-pumped tunable laser oscillators can be constructed with narrow linewidths, high conversion efficiencies, and low background amplified spontaneous emission intensity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of high power, narrow linewidth, tunable laser oscillators.
the development of a high repetition rate, high average power dye laser system for use in a high resolution, high sensitivity, high speed, tunable, narrow-bandwidth laser absorption spectrometer.
the development of high power, narrow linewidth dye-lasers pumped by copper lasers for applications in spectroscopy, holography, and laser radar.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dye laser system described here is an efficient, reliable, and versatile source of narrow-bandwidth radiation in the 570–600-nm wavelength range.
the dye laser system has a number of advantages over other systems for a variety of applications.
these dye laser oscillators are the best of their class.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Littrow-mounted grating configuration is a good design for a narrow linewidth, high prl copper laser pumped dye-laser oscillator, but the grazing-incidence-grating configuration is better for a low background amplified spontaneous emission, narrow linewidth, high pulse repetition frequency copper laser-pumped laser oscillator.
the dye laser can be operated with high prf and narrow linewidths, and the background ASE is very small.
the grazing-incidence-grating cavity is a better choice for high prf, high-efficiency dye-laser oscillation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of double-prism beam expander in conjunction with a grazing-incidence grater in the oscillator cavity is a simple, effective means to reduce the linewidth and increase the output power of a high-repetition-rate dye laser pumped by a copper laser.
high prf copper lasers are a viable alternative to flash-lamp-pumped dye lasers in many applications.
the grazing-incidence cavity is superior for narrow linewidth, high prfs, and that the Littrow cavity has advantages for high prf and high power.
